correctness.rationale: The complete 66/180/117-cell signed deleted-product chain complex is independently enumerated from the specified LCF graph and satisfies the integral cellular boundary identities. Exact exhaustive simple-cycle enumeration yields 19 vertex-disjoint cycle pairs, each with zero integral product boundary. Rank 108 modulo 101 gives a rational upper bound nine for second homology, while a verified unit determinant +1 for nine explicit torus chains gives rank at least nine and a primitive rank-nine integral sublattice of the whole \(C_2\). Therefore this sublattice is exactly \(\ker\partial_2\) over \(\mathbb Z\). Inversion of this integral minor reconstructs all 19 product chains; exact rational lattice ranks and explicit unit minors establish all partial free quotients and the sharp need for three hexagon–hexagon classes. All 48 automorphisms are enumerated and torus-orbit transitivity verified. Evidence: included verify_franklin.py and its output; finite experiments alone are not extrapolated to arbitrary graphs.

value.rationale: For the distinguished nonplanar Franklin graph with a Klein-bottle map interpretation, the integral geometric generation problem is naturally different from the planar torus-generation theorem. The result resolves all 19 disjoint-cycle product tori into three symmetry orbits and exact integral lattice subgroups, and establishes a sharp necessity/sufficiency of three hexagon-pair tori for a nine-class basis. Square-square cycles become redundant in the square-hexagon lattice, while four-cycle-bearing tori alone miss three free homology directions. This is a motivated complete integral classification rather than a bare Betti count, arbitrary slice, or a standard substitution into a published formula; no large-family theorem is asserted.
